summary: Let the per-column options of `tabulate()` take a dict keyed by header name, so a caller can set the format or alignment of one column without counting columns.
behaviour: `colalign`, `floatfmt`, `intfmt`, `missingval` and `maxcolwidths` also accept a dict that maps header names to the value for that column. The names are the headers `tabulate()` prints, so this works with a list of headers, `headers="keys"` and `headers="firstrow"`, and with an index column from `showindex`.
Columns the dict does not name get the usual default: their normal alignment for `colalign`, `"g"` for `floatfmt`, `""` for `intfmt` and `missingval`, and no width limit for `maxcolwidths`.
When several columns have the same header, the value applies to every one of them.
A name that is not one of the table's headers raises `ValueError`, so a dict on a table without headers always raises.
Lists, tuples and single values work as before.

entries: - Added: maxcolwidths, maxheadercolwidths and rowalign accept tuples, and extra per-column values are ignored. (feature/27c90a)
- Changed: maxcolwidths also wraps the headers when maxheadercolwidths is not given. (feature/9d41b7)
